concept: A button is a small pane lit from above. Its fill is a sheet lit at its top and shaded at its foot, it carries the top-lit rim, and a glint sits where the pointer is. Loud is the white solid (ink in light); the promoted accent is the same solid glowing with its own light. One loud kind per pane.

root.why: a small pane, a full pill with the pane rim brightest at the top left, held as an object with the whole pill as the target

sm.why: small is 32px for dense rows and toolbars where several actions share a line

md.why: medium is the default 44px touch size, used for every action that is not in a dense row

light.why: the loud solid, the one opaque mark on a pane, white in dark and ink in light, lit at its top and shaded at its foot, resting on its own shadow

accent.why: the promoted action is the loud solid glowing with its own light onto the pane, never beside another loud solid

glass.why: quiet glass lit from above, brighter at its top, resting on a short soft shadow; it does not lift

hit.why: a press area at least 44px each way, so the small size is still easy to hit

content.why: the label stays in place unseen while loading so the button keeps its width and nothing jumps

loading.why: a busy button keeps focus, says it is busy and ignores presses until the action is done

spinner.why: the spinner sits over the hidden label so the reader sees the action is still running

ghost.why: the ghost button is the label alone so a third action never competes with the loud one

danger.why: a destructive action keeps quiet glass and takes the critical mark on its label, as in Menu and ActionSheet

lg.why: the large size is 56px for the one action of a screen, easy to reach with a thumb

full.why: a full-width button fills its container for the single action at the foot of a sheet or form

icon.why: a glyph beside the label is hidden from screen readers so the label alone says the action

hover.why: hover lifts the loud kinds two pixels closer and shows the glint under the pointer on every kind

active.why: a press shrinks the button and tightens its shadow, faster than hover, so it is pushed back toward the pane

disabled.why: disabled uses the native attribute and the shared disabled opacity, and the reason is written near it

focus-visible.why: keyboard focus draws the shared ring with its halo so the focused control is visible on any scene

@media forced-colors: active.why: forced colours drop rim, glint and fills, so a real system-colour border keeps the shape

transform.why: lift and press both move by transform over the soft curve so they never shift layout

box-shadow.why: the shadow spreads with the lift and tightens on press, so the button rises off the pane and is pushed back

opacity.why: the glint fades in and out at hover pace, answering the pointer arriving and leaving

default_to_avoid.pattern: a flat brand-coloured rounded button with a grey drop shadow (Bootstrap .btn-primary, Material filled button, most Tailwind kits)
default_to_avoid.why_not: it is a coloured sticker on the glass with no edge, no light and no weight, so on a pane floating in a scene it reads as a web page pasted in front of the world (R-010)

derivation.consequence: light falls from above, so every surface carries a rim brightest along its top edge and a soft shadow below that says where it floats, and a recess is the inverse, shaded under its top lip and lit on its bottom lip
derivation.form: a button is a pane at a smaller scale, so it carries the same top-left rim and rests on a shadow of its own

derivation.consequence: the rim and sheen are white at low opacity, like light catching an edge
derivation.form: the fill is a sheet with a white gloss across its top and a shade at its foot; the rim is white, never a coloured border

derivation.consequence: the solid fill sits on top of the glass and is the only opaque mark on a pane
derivation.form: loud and accent stay opaque (tinted glass, variant C, was rejected); the quiet button is glass with gloss and no shadow

derivation.consequence: only the loud action lifts with a shadow
derivation.form: only loud and accent lift on hover; the accent also glows with its own light, the only glow on a pane

derivation.consequence: nothing moves on its own; every motion answers something the reader did
derivation.form: a glint sits under the pointer and follows it, the visionOS hover effect, and is gone when the pointer leaves

derivation.consequence: a pressed control shrinks slightly, as something pushed
derivation.form: a press shrinks the button and tightens its shadow, so it is pushed back toward the pane

options: B a small pane of coloured glass
variants.picked: B a small pane of coloured glass
variants.reason: B is the only one that takes P3 at its word: the button carries the pane's own rim and sheen, so it reads as a smaller sheet of the same material instead of a sticker. A has the sheet but no rim and no answer to the pointer (P4 interaction). C breaks P5 (the loud fill must be opaque) and measured white text at 2.6:1 on light glass, against P2.

options: C A with a spectral edge
round4.reason: The user rejected the blue and showed a reference where one light from above lights every atom alike. A reads that straight: the same top rim and sheen on every surface, the white lit solid for the loud action, chosen items as lighter glass. B makes chosen items recesses, which reads as pressed-off rather than chosen. C adds a rainbow edge, a hue the system no longer owns (P1).
